articles.title: Account security and passkeys
articles.description: Admin → Settings → Security
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Security Add a passkey Open security settings on a compatible browser and register a passkey using the device prompt. Verify it appears in your account list. Sign in with a passkey Use the passkey sign-in option and complete the browser/device verification. A device unlock does not grant restaurant permissions you do not already hold. Remove an unused key Select an unused passkey in security settings and confirm removal. Keep a working sign-in method before removing your last key. If the operation fails If the device prompt fails, keep the existing key and use another configured sign-in method.

articles.title: Subscription and billing status
articles.description: Admin → Account → Billing, when offered
articles.body: Admin → Account → Billing, when offered Read the current subscription Check the recorded plan, subscription status and relevant trial/renewal/grace date. Confirm commercial terms with Foody; technical plan labels can differ from current offers. Review a plan change An authorized owner reviews and confirms an offered plan change. Wait for the subscription reread; if uncertain, verify the recorded plan before submitting again. Review billing events Inspect event type, date, amount and currency. Contact support for an unexplained failed payment or blocked subscription; an order payment is separate from the software subscription.

articles.title: Restaurant business assistant
articles.description: Open the AI business panel in Admin with an authorized restaurant account. This panel is distinct from the public help assistant.
articles.body: Open the AI business panel in Admin with an authorized restaurant account. This panel is distinct from the public help assistant. Ask about business data Choose the intended restaurant and ask a precise question about current/weekly sales, top items, stock, recent orders, customers, staff or menu. Review the answer against the relevant source screen. AI interpretation is not proof of payment reconciliation or a substitute for accounting. Understand the panel’s scope Available business queries use the signed-in restaurant context. The public support assistant receives only published guides and conversation. Do not paste business/customer exports, passwords or card details into public support. If a business answer is unsupported, use the source module or contact an authorized manager.

articles.title: Read your dashboard and reports
articles.description: Choose the date basis and understand which orders are counted.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Start from Home Open Home in FoodyAdmin. The dashboard shows the selected period or service, the orders requiring attention, gross sales, order count, average order value, items sold and recent orders. What you can open depends on your permissions. Check the date basis The date control can use order dates or a scheduled service/series. A future service can include orders already placed for that service: those figures do not mean that service has been completed. Check the date basis before comparing figures with another report. The orders counted control indicates the revenue calculation, such as paid orders or accepted orders. Accepted-order sales are not proof that all payments were collected. Review payment attention separately. Comparisons and unavailable data Comparisons depend on an available previous period or service. For a future or ongoing service, the dashboard explains why a comparison is not shown. Unavailable data and an empty period are different; use Refresh or resolve the reported load error before interpreting missing figures as zero. Detailed reports Open Reports for the reporting pages your role permits. Select the date range and review the applied filters. The overview provides an export action; export the selected scope and check that its dates and calculation match your intended analysis.

articles.title: Catering branches and routing
articles.description: Open Catering → Branches and Routing.
articles.body: Open Catering → Branches and Routing. Maintain eligible branches Create or edit the branch’s available fields and active state. Check its restaurant ownership and service associations. An inactive branch should not be used as a new customer destination. Set routing rules Create/edit a rule using the offered service, destination and conditions. Review priority/order and conflicts before saving. Check a representative request against the rules, and confirm before deleting a rule that existing workflows rely on.

articles.title: Catering events and balance collection
articles.description: Open Catering → Events and the intended event.
articles.body: Open Catering → Events and the intended event. Review the accepted event Check date/time, branch, guests, configuration, status and recorded payments. Use the available event actions only after checking production needs and assignments. Quote approval, event progress and payment status are distinct. Manage a supported balance authorization Open the balance panel and read its current state. Create/share a link or settle only when the displayed action is allowed by the provider and event state. Refresh/reconcile an ambiguous authorization before another operation. Do not treat an authorization as captured money.

articles.title: Catering questions, scheduling and pricing
articles.description: In the service editor open customer flow and pricing. Use the simulator before publishing.
articles.body: In the service editor open customer flow and pricing. Use the simulator before publishing. Configure customer steps Maintain step order, required questions and single-choice options. Configure scheduling, guest count, event details and selections supported by the service. Check translated labels and every branch of the flow; changing a question can affect pricing conditions. Maintain pricing rules Choose the item, base/fallback rate and conditional rules such as guest count, weekday, slot or a selected answer. Avoid overlapping specific rules. In the simulator choose a representative context and inspect the resolved rate and any conflict warning before saving.

articles.title: Review catering quotes
articles.description: Open Catering → Quotes and select the request. Review its current status and full configuration.
articles.body: Open Catering → Quotes and select the request. Review its current status and full configuration. Approve or reject a quote Check customer request, event date, guests, selections, calculated total and deposit status. If permitted adjust the total and add a note, then approve or reject explicitly. Confirm the saved status; a request awaiting review is not an accepted event. Review deposit and refund evidence Distinguish the primary deposit from a recorded duplicate charge. If Refund is available, select the intended target and amount and confirm once. For an external refund, first complete it in the provider console, then record its required reference in Foody. Recording an external refund does not itself move money. An uncertain provider result requires review before retrying.

articles.title: Catering services, catalog and offers
articles.description: Open Catering → Services, choose a service and its catalog/offer panels.
articles.body: Open Catering → Services, choose a service and its catalog/offer panels. Create and activate a service Create the service with name, description, slug and available languages, then review active state, quote mode and deposit policy. Save before adding its public page. An active service still needs the appropriate public configuration and availability. Maintain groups and items Add service catalog groups and items, edit descriptions, images/gallery, active state and pricing data. Review allowed selections and portion/guest quantities. This catering catalog is separate from ordinary POS menu groups; verify the service context before editing. Build offers and formulas Create/edit the service offer, its included items and choice constraints. Preview the configured customer flow and total. Do not publish an offer until all selectable items, quantities and required choices have been checked.

articles.title: Chains and branch management
articles.description: Open Chain/Branches or the chain dashboard with an authorized account.
articles.body: Open Chain/Branches or the chain dashboard with an authorized account. Choose the right branch Select the chain and branch, then verify the active restaurant context before editing menu, stock, staff or payments. Shared chain presentation does not make restaurant records interchangeable. Review public branch presence Maintain branch information and available website/ordering presence, then check the chain selector and branch destination. Confirm active menus, hours, fulfillment and payment configuration independently for each restaurant before publication.

articles.title: Message templates and workflow automation
articles.description: Open Settings → Message templates, WhatsApp templates or Order workflow according to the channel.
articles.body: Open Settings → Message templates, WhatsApp templates or Order workflow according to the channel. Create and review a template Edit supported localized text and variables, or submit a WhatsApp Utility template through the supported provider. Check approval, language and the positional variable contract before selection. Deleting a referenced template can be blocked even when its workflow stage is disabled. Attach messages to workflow stages Select an approved template on the intended stage and choose its supported timing. Stage-entry messages apply to future entries, not historical orders. Delivery reminders need saved delivery/courier data; satisfaction messages require recorded fulfillment. Read the selected trigger rather than assuming every reminder is sent the day before. Assign the file to a notification After approval, open Configure on the WhatsApp message, or Notify customer in Settings → Restaurant → Order workflow. Choose the photo/PDF model and then its fixed file from this restaurant’s library, or Receipt for this order for a PDF model. Save the page or workflow; Done only closes the general-message configuration panel. The workflow’s selected trigger and timing remain authoritative. Foody generates the receipt from the saved items and amounts for that order; it does not replace a tax invoice. Review the message and file previews before a manual send. Each message has one attachment, using activated direct Meta routing; these controls do not configure Twilio attachments. Review a route-based delivery reminder For an assigned delivery with a saved customer-window setting, reminders use the route arrival plus the configured duration, rather than the order’s broad scheduled slot. For example, arrival at 08:30 and 90 minutes produces 08:30–10:00. Configure it in Orders → Deliveries → allocation, beside the time at each stop, and review the manual or approved WhatsApp preview before sending. The same range supplies Twilio, Meta and stage reminders; existing template variables and J-1 eligibility remain in effect. Unconfigured historic routes keep the original saved slot. If the range cannot be verified, recalculate the route and reopen the reminder. A changed approved preview must be reviewed again before sending. Editing a template alone does not calculate a route or change its margin.

articles.title: Connect and operate WhatsApp
articles.description: Open Settings → WhatsApp. Select the supported connection/billing mode before entering credentials.
articles.body: Open Settings → WhatsApp. Select the supported connection/billing mode before entering credentials. Connect a sender Use Foody-managed connection or the restaurant’s personal Twilio account if offered. A personal sender must already be registered and online with approved Utility templates belonging to the same account. Enter secrets only in the protected form. A failed verification preserves the prior configuration; switching billing modes requires disconnecting first. Use a gated Meta coexistence connection Direct Meta coexistence is a controlled pilot and disabled by default. Connecting alone does not switch message routing; activate the intended provider explicitly after verification. The existing Business app remains available. Do not assume fallback to Twilio if a Meta send fails. Read message history In the order’s communication panel inspect sent, delivered, read, failed and blocked-before-send records. A blocked automation is not proof of delivery. For a reviewed courier reminder use its explicit action only when eligible. Unknown provider outcomes are not automatically replayed; investigate before another send. Create a model with a photo or PDF In Settings → Communications → WhatsApp, a user with settings-edit permission can open Create a model. Choose the notification type, language and a new name, then Message attachment: Photo or PDF document. Upload a JPEG/PNG up to 5 MB for a photo, or a PDF up to 10 MB for a fixed document. For each order’s own receipt, choose PDF document then Document to send → Receipt for this order. The server uses a fictional sample document for Meta approval. Review the text and submit. Wait for Utility approval before assigning the model to a notification. An existing text-only model cannot gain an attachment afterward; create a new model with the required header type. Manage files and check sends Files are available to authorized restaurant users through attachment configuration, without a public storage link. Preview file opens an authenticated preview. Delete file requires confirmation and refuses files referenced by a notification, saved stage or pending message. Replace the file in those settings and save first. The library allows 40 files and 100 MB per restaurant. If upload or deletion is unconfirmed, refresh the list before retrying. If transfer to Meta fails, Foody does not send the text alone or switch to Twilio. In the order → Customer messages, check the attachment filename recorded with the attempt and the status returned by WhatsApp; Read depends on WhatsApp’s return. Review a route-based delivery reminder For an assigned delivery with a saved customer-window setting, reminders use the route arrival plus the configured duration, rather than the order’s broad scheduled slot. For example, arrival at 08:30 and 90 minutes produces 08:30–10:00. Configure it in Orders → Deliveries → allocation, beside the time at each stop, and review the manual or approved WhatsApp preview before sending. The same range supplies Twilio, Meta and stage reminders; existing template variables and J-1 eligibility remain in effect. Unconfigured historic routes keep the original saved slot. If the range cannot be verified, recalculate the route and reopen the reminder. A changed approved preview must be reviewed again before sending. Editing a template alone does not calculate a route or change its margin.

articles.title: Customers, addresses and duplicates
articles.description: Admin → Clients
articles.body: Admin → Clients Availability and access Editing and merging require customer-management permission. Find a customer Search the customer list and inspect name, phone, address, order count and last order. Check the intended person before editing. Edit delivery details Open the customer profile, correct the phone/address and delivery details, then save. Recheck the selected order address separately for already-created orders. Authorize cash ordering Use the trusted/cash-allowed setting only for the intended customer. This controls cash ordering eligibility, not evidence of an actual payment. Merge duplicates Review selected customer profiles and phone numbers before confirming a merge. Check the resulting combined profile and avoid merging different people.

articles.title: Courier itinerary and delivery completion
articles.description: Admin → Orders → Courier mode, or assigned courier workspace
articles.body: Admin → Orders → Courier mode, or assigned courier workspace Open the assigned itinerary Open the assigned route and check its date, stop sequence and delivery windows. Use only orders assigned to your authorized courier context. Navigate and contact Open an offered navigation app for the stop and review customer contact/delivery instructions. Check a corrected address with dispatch before changing the delivery plan. Confirm the actual result Use the offered stop/order status action after the actual handover. Record required information and verify the saved result; a delivery confirmation does not by itself collect an unpaid balance. Edit endpoints and start the route Before departure, open Edit on your assigned route. Set departure time, departure address and final destination; use the address suggestions or enter a complete address manually. Set the customer window and handover duration separately, then save and review the recalculated sequence. Changing an endpoint resets manual ordering. Start route confirms that the assigned unfinished deliveries are leaving and changes accepted, preparing and ready deliveries together to Out for delivery. Finished/cancelled deliveries are not reopened. A held kitchen course or an unsettled weight order must be resolved first. If departure fails, no partial status change is saved. A courier can have only one active route; finish it before starting another. Before departure, departure and final addresses remain editable after allocation. Include the house number, street and city; the number may appear before or after the street name, and the displayed address is retained. If Address not found appears, check the number and city, then select another suggestion or correct the full address. A temporary location-service failure requires trying again later. The saved route remains unchanged on either failure. When Google is active in Maps and routes, departure and final addresses can use a precise Google match even when Geoapify cannot locate them. Save the route settings before departure and review the recalculated final leg. If Google is unavailable or its protected quota is exhausted and the other provider cannot locate an endpoint, saving or recalculation is blocked and the previous plan is retained; the final destination is never silently omitted. Google-only points are shown on the Google map and hidden when the map switches provider. Select a precisely located alternative or try again when Google becomes available.

articles.title: Dispatch and route planning
articles.description: Admin → Orders → Deliveries / Delivery tours
articles.body: Admin → Orders → Deliveries / Delivery tours Refund or void a Verifone online payment The Admin order payment section supports total or partial matched refunds and total VOID for an eligible single Verifone online payment, for owners/managers with payments.manage. Provider state, captured amount and verified history govern eligibility, not a fixed 24-hour rule. This does not cancel preparation or fulfillment and does not add a POS terminal refund button. Unknown results stay reserved and must be checked, never resubmitted. Invoice4U credit/cancellation documents require a separate check. See the online payment procedure. A captured ABS sale still AUTHORISED/AUTHORIZED or SETTLEMENT REQUESTED is not settled: Admin shows Available to void and only Void entire payment, with no prior refund. Refund payment and Available to refund require an explicit settled state or verified partially-refunded history. Generic APPROVED/COMPLETED, contradictory states or missing evidence offer neither action. A state change before confirmation rejects the stale action; it never switches VOID to REFUND automatically. Request rejected by Verifone means no return of funds is confirmed, not necessarily an issuer decline. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. Select deliveries for one date Choose the route date and review available delivery orders. Do not combine scheduled deliveries from another service date into the route. Assign couriers and stops Select the intended courier, depot and orders, then review stop addresses, service times and promised windows. Correct an address before optimization. Review a calculated route Run the offered route calculation or fleet allocation and inspect the result before saving/dispatching. Review driving, waiting and handover duration separately; recalculations may consume provider usage. Save and track progress Save the reviewed route and use the dispatch controls. Monitor courier/order progress and update a changed plan deliberately instead of assuming the original route remains valid. Set each courier’s departure and final address With the matching API and Admin release installed, select deliveries and couriers in Orders → Deliveries → allocation. Enter each courier’s departure and final destination before generating the plan. Type at least three characters and select an address suggestion; street-only results require a house number. If suggestions are unavailable, enter the complete address manually and save to locate it. The final address can be the courier’s home. Foody optimizes the deliveries between these endpoints, while retaining existing delivery-window constraints. For a departure near Tel Aviv and a final home in Netanya, review that Herzliya and Raanana precede Netanya. Before departure, the admin or assigned courier can edit the route settings and save; changing either endpoint resets a manual stop order and recalculates the route. A failed address lookup leaves the saved plan unchanged. Before departure, departure and final addresses remain editable after allocation. Include the house number, street and city; the number may appear before or after the street name, and the displayed address is retained. If Address not found appears, check the number and city, then select another suggestion or correct the full address. A temporary location-service failure requires trying again later. The saved route remains unchanged on either failure. When Google is active in Maps and routes, departure and final addresses can use a precise Google match even when Geoapify cannot locate them. Save the route settings before departure and review the recalculated final leg. If Google is unavailable or its protected quota is exhausted and the other provider cannot locate an endpoint, saving or recalculation is blocked and the previous plan is retained; the final destination is never silently omitted. Google-only points are shown on the Google map and hidden when the map switches provider. Select a precisely located alternative or try again when Google becomes available. Set the customer delivery range In allocation, use Customer delivery window beside Time at each stop. New plans propose 90 minutes. Enter 1:30, 1h30 or 90 for an hour and a half; the allowed range is 1–720 minutes. The range begins at the calculated arrival, rounded down to its displayed minute: 08:30 plus 90 minutes gives 08:30–10:00. It does not extend the handover time or change the order’s original scheduling constraints. The setting is saved per route and can be edited before departure. Delivery WhatsApp links and manual/approved reminders use this range. Reopen a reminder after recalculation to review its updated text. Historic routes without this setting retain their saved reminder slot. If a configured route cannot provide a valid arrival, recalculate or correct its address before sending; no guessed range is substituted. Attach a file to a WhatsApp reminder With direct Meta notifications enabled, configure the attachment in Settings → Communications → WhatsApp or on the Order workflow stage: an approved photo/PDF header template, an authorized fixed file or that order’s PDF receipt. This selection changes neither the route nor the configured sending time. Review the file in the manual preview and the attachment filename in Customer messages; a filename does not prove delivery. Make a one-order combo exception For a one-order combo exception, an authorized Admin user opens the combo step and selects Choose another item. The replacement is included without a surcharge and is saved on that order only. Fulfillment, scheduling and delivery rules remain unchanged. Review the selected dish and portion in the order details. Guest and POS combo pickers retain the configured composition; arrange an exception through the internal Admin order editor. See the combo guide for quantities, eligibility and recovery. Keep stock provenance when moving fulfillment Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters. Access the new controls Settings → Usage and quotas displays this restaurant’s Google/Geoapify allowances and usage with settings view/edit permission. Fallback credits and deliveries submitted for optimization are distinct from request counts. Foody adjusts limits without resetting counters. See limits and renewal.

articles.title: Maps providers and usage
articles.description: Admin → Settings → Delivery → Maps
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Delivery → Maps Review the configured map provider Read the active provider and available usage information. Keep provider credentials in the designated secure configuration; never paste them into support chat. When Google is active in Maps and routes, departure and final addresses can use a precise Google match even when Geoapify cannot locate them. Save the route settings before departure and review the recalculated final leg. If Google is unavailable or its protected quota is exhausted and the other provider cannot locate an endpoint, saving or recalculation is blocked and the previous plan is retained; the final destination is never silently omitted. Google-only points are shown on the Google map and hidden when the map switches provider. Select a precisely located alternative or try again when Google becomes available. Respect usage limits Check map, address-search and route/optimization limits before large planning sessions. A commercial offer does not automatically activate an extra quota or bypass a provider cap. Access the new controls Settings → Usage and quotas displays this restaurant’s Google/Geoapify allowances and usage with settings view/edit permission. Fallback credits and deliveries submitted for optimization are distinct from request counts. Foody adjusts limits without resetting counters. See limits and renewal.

articles.title: Delivery zones, fees and calendars
articles.description: Admin → Settings → Delivery
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Delivery Create a delivery zone Create or edit a named zone using the map/address controls. Review its area, active state and ordering eligibility before saving. Set fees and minimums Set the offered fee and minimum-order rules for the zone. Test an address and basket on each boundary; the delivery fee is separate from external courier charges. Configure delivery days and windows Set the zone schedule and offered delivery windows. Where final times are pending, keep that pending state and confirm the real window later from order planning.

articles.title: Set up your restaurant with Foody
articles.description: A practical order for reviewing account access, menus, devices and online ordering.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Review the setup with your Foody representative 1. Activate your account and select the right restaurant. Sign in. 2. Review the restaurant profile, opening hours and order/service settings for your actual operation. 3. Create catalogue items, then place them in customer-facing menu groups. Check channels, hours, prices, variants and modifiers. Items and menus. 4. Review staff roles, employee invitations and activated POS devices. Staff access. 5. If you use online ordering, review the website draft, publish it and check the public ordering link. Website publishing. 6. Confirm your payment provider and receipt/printing setup with Foody before taking live orders. Payment status. 7. Test the intended order flow using the agreed test environment, including preparation and handover. Confirm payment results separately from order status. The enabled modules, hardware and payment methods depend on your installation and contract. Ask Foody to confirm the setup rather than assuming every option is available. Do not submit live payments as test transactions.

articles.title: Sign in and recover access
articles.description: Access the Admin and the POS with your own restaurant account.
articles.body: Admin sign-in and account menu Activate an invitation Open the received invitation, check the restaurant and finish account setup. Ask the manager to resend an expired invitation. Select the restaurant Sign in with your own account, then choose an authorized restaurant. Check its name before editing or exporting data. Recover access Follow the account recovery instructions or contact your manager. Never share a password, activation link or POS code in the assistant. End a POS shift safely On an enrolled POS, choose End shift. If Foody reports an open cash drawer, use the offered shortcut to More → Reports → Cash drawer balance. Count and close the drawer on that same device, then retry End shift. A Verifone terminal deposit is separate. If cash or payment confirmation is uncertain, ask an authorized manager to reconcile it before ending the shift; do not bypass the guard by logging out another way.

articles.title: How it all connects: from ingredients to a sold-out dish
articles.description: The big picture — how stock, preparations, recipes, items, availability, food cost and orders fit together, and the order to set them up.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. The big picture Six pieces work together. Once you understand the chain, everything else clicks: - Stock — the raw ingredients you buy (tomatoes, tuna, oil, buns). - Preparations — things you make from stock in batches (a sauce, a dough, a marinade). - Recipe — what one dish uses: its ingredients and preparations, with quantities. - Item (article) — a dish on your menu, shown to customers inside a menu group. - Availability — computed from the recipe + current stock: low stock or sold-out, automatically. - Food cost — also computed from the recipe. The flow: Stock ┐ ├─→ Recipe ─→ Item ─→ shown to customers Preps ┘ │ ├─→ Availability (low / sold-out, automatic) └─→ Food cost (margin per dish) An order is placed ─→ the recipe is deducted from Stock ─→ Availability updates So a dish isn't an island: it points at a recipe, the recipe points at stock and preparations, and that single link makes availability and food cost work on their own. Set it up in this order Set it up in this order 1. Add your ingredients to Stock Enter the raw ingredients you buy, with their unit and current quantity. → Stock management 2. (Optional) Build your Preparations If you make sauces, doughs or bases in batches, define them once and reuse them across dishes. Producing a batch credits stock; dishes that use it recover automatically. → Preparations 3. Create your items Add each dish to your catalogue (name, price, photo, category). → Creating a menu item 4. Give each item a recipe On the item's Recipe and cost section, link the ingredients and preparations one portion uses, with quantities. This is the link that powers everything downstream. A dish with no recipe is not enough to compute ingredient consumption; check manual availability overrides separately. → Ingredients & portions 5. Put items in a menu group Items only appear to customers once they're in a menu group. → Categories & items 6. Availability now works on its own With recipes in place, dishes go low stock and sold out automatically as stock runs down, and come back when you restock. Tune it with rules, or override a single dish. → Availability What you get once the chain is connected - Automatic sold-out — no more manually switching dishes off when an ingredient runs out. - Accurate food cost — margin per dish, rolled up from the recipe. - Self-updating stock — every order deducts its recipe, so your numbers stay honest. - One place to change things — update a preparation's recipe once and every dish follows. Where to go next - Take and manage orders → Managing orders - Get paid → How payments work - First-time setup checklist → Complete setup guide

articles.title: Offers, demo and contacting Foody
articles.description: Visit foody-pos.co.il, choose French, Hebrew or English, then Products, Pricing, Demo or Contact.
articles.body: Visit foody-pos.co.il, choose French, Hebrew or English, then Products, Pricing, Demo or Contact. Compare public offers Review the published POS, Orders, Restaurant, Kitchen and combined offers and their inclusions. Companion belongs to Kitchen. Device licenses cover devices, not a separate charge per employee. Check the current approved pricing page and scoped quote for hardware, external processing, SMS and integrations. Request a demo or support Use Demo/Contact with the requested business contact details and wait for the success confirmation. The Help center is public at /fr/help, /he/help and /en/help. Its assistant answers published procedures and cannot access or change a restaurant account. Do not send secrets or card data.

articles.title: Search and navigate FoodyAdmin
articles.description: Use the search entry in the Admin navigation for the currently selected restaurant.
articles.body: Use the search entry in the Admin navigation for the currently selected restaurant. Find a business record Open search, enter a sufficiently specific term and review grouped item, order, customer and stock results. Use arrows and Enter to open, or Escape to close. Results respect the current restaurant and permissions; an empty result is not proof the record never existed. Filter and inspect a list Use the page’s search, filters, date range, column chooser and pagination where available. Open the row/action menu for its permitted operations. Check active filters before treating a missing record as deleted. Transactions is a separate Admin sidebar destination for confirmed payments; the global search groups items, orders, customers and stock, but is not a payment-history search. Find the item-stock overview Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Using Foody help and the assistant
articles.description: Find a guide, ask a question and contact support from FoodyAdmin.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Find a guide Select Help and support at the bottom of the FoodyAdmin navigation. Open help center opens the guides in a new tab. The public help center also works without signing in. Search a question or browse topics, including items and menus, orders, kitchen, payments, hardware, staff and settings. Search includes article text. Select English, French or Hebrew in the header. Articles awaiting translation remain available in English. Ask a question 1. Open the assistant. 2. Write a question or select a suggestion. 3. Read the answer and open its Sources to check the procedure. 4. Ask a follow-up question. New conversation clears the panel. The assistant explains documented Foody features. It cannot view your account or orders and cannot perform actions. In Admin, the current topic helps find relevant articles; restaurant records and sign-in credentials are not forwarded. Answers can contain errors. Do not share passwords, payment details or personal customer information. Questions and recent conversation turns are sent to our AI provider. The conversation stays in the browser tab's memory; reloading clears it. For receipt or confirmation link previews, ask a general question about the restaurant name or logo and open the cited guide. The assistant uses the published procedure; it cannot open your private link or inspect the order. Do not paste receipt or tracking links into the conversation. For example, ask how to add an item outside the active menus to a staff order. Check the Article library steps in the order guide; the assistant cannot inspect your restaurant’s items or add them to an order. Ask where to find payment history The assistant can point you to the published Transactions procedure for confirmed POS and online payments. It cannot see your restaurant's transactions, inspect a card, confirm an uncertain charge or initiate a refund. Open the actual Transactions screen with the required permission, or ask an authorized operator to reconcile a missing payment before retrying. Contact support Select Contact support to write to support@foody-pos.co.il. Include the product, steps and error message, with sensitive information removed. Sending the email remains an action in your email application. If the assistant is unavailable or its question limit is reached, guides and the support contact remain accessible. Report a procedure that differs from your screen The assistant cannot see your screen or account. If a named button or section no longer exists, give the product, language and guide title, then contact support to correct the procedure. Do not share credentials or customer/payment data. An existing citation alone does not guarantee that every step matches the latest interface. Panel placement can change with language and screen width. Locate a control by its label and documented section rather than an assumed side. In the item editor, the visible side-card headings are Status, Categories and Menus. A suggestion or draft is not a send: purchase generation and supplier transmission are separate actions requiring manual confirmation. Follow the labels displayed in your language: Items & menus → Item library. A question may call this Menu → Items; use the displayed path when following the answer and report a different label. Find delivery planning guidance The delivery guides cover departure/final address suggestions, route order towards the final destination, starting all assigned deliveries together and the customer reminder range. Search for delivery customer window or open Delivery → Dispatch and route planning. Check the installed release before following newly added controls. The assistant cites the same published guides; it cannot inspect a courier’s route, change an order or send WhatsApp messages. Find WhatsApp attachment guidance Read Communications → WhatsApp and Message templates to configure a photo, fixed PDF or order PDF receipt with Meta. The guides and assistant use the same published procedure. The assistant explains documented controls; it cannot open private files, inspect orders or confirm message delivery. Check those details in Foody. Make a one-order combo exception Ask “How can I replace beef with fish in an internal combo without a surcharge?” The assistant should cite the combo or order guide, explain Choose another item and required orders.manage access, and distinguish the one-order exception from editing the saved definition. It cannot inspect or edit your actual order. Find the mobile address procedure For trouble entering or choosing an address on a phone, search for address or delivery in Help and open Order online as a customer. The assistant cites the same guide in an available language. Check its source and the site release; if the procedure is missing or differs from your screen, contact the restaurant without sharing customer details or payment data with the assistant. On mobile, Pickup and Delivery tabs, the field and the Sign in link at the top keep their positions when the keyboard opens or closes. Compact suggestions show the address and city on two lines in a larger scrolling list. During search, confirmation leaves room for suggestions; it appears after choosing a complete address. The cover is reserved for larger screens. Google Maps attribution and errors stay visible. For a street suggestion without a house number, follow the guide to add the number and choose the complete address; a street alone does not confirm delivery. Find stock movement history To investigate a quantity change, read Availability. Items & menus → Stock history displays movements only, with item, series-date and movement-type filters. Quantities are prepared from the carte. The assistant explains this public procedure without reading your stock or orders. Help with quotas and optional sign-in Help documents restaurant Google/Geoapify usage, monthly limits and renewal under Usage and quotas. It also explains the published sign-in invitation setting and Order without an account. The assistant uses the same public guides: it can explain procedures but cannot read your counters, change allowances or publish your site.

articles.title: Submit a catering request
articles.description: Open the restaurant’s Catering service or a delivery-tour/preorder link.
articles.body: Open the restaurant’s Catering service or a delivery-tour/preorder link. Complete a catering flow Select the active service/offer and complete guest count, date/time, choices and contact details. Review the calculated total and whether approval or deposit is required. Submit once and retain the private quote link. A quote awaiting approval is not final acceptance. Order for a specific tour Check the tour’s fulfillment date, ordering window and cutoff before building the basket. A closed/unavailable tour cannot be bypassed with a stale page. Confirm the displayed route/fulfillment information before payment.

articles.title: Order online as a customer
articles.description: Open the restaurant’s public link or select a branch from its chain page.
articles.body: Open the restaurant’s public link or select a branch from its chain page. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. Build a basket Choose pickup, delivery or table ordering when offered, select the active menu and open an item. Choose a variant, required modifiers, quantity and allowed notes, then add it. Review and edit the basket before checkout. A customer assistant suggestion still needs the same required choices and availability checks. Choose an address on a phone In the ordering dialog, choose Delivery and enter the street, house number and city. If address search is enabled, scroll the suggestions and tap the complete address. Selecting a street still requires its house number and keeps the keyboard open. A complete address dismisses the keyboard; review any offered times and tap Confirm address. The button stays disabled while checks run or delivery is unavailable. For pickup, choose Pickup then Confirm pickup. The cross at the top closes the dialog. Account access remains optional. If no address matches, refine the number or city; if the service fails, retry or contact the restaurant. On mobile, Pickup and Delivery tabs, the field and the Sign in link at the top keep their positions when the keyboard opens or closes. Compact suggestions show the address and city on two lines in a larger scrolling list. During search, confirmation leaves room for suggestions; it appears after choosing a complete address. The cover is reserved for larger screens. Google Maps attribution and errors stay visible. After choosing a street, add the house number in the same field and choose the complete address suggestion. A street alone cannot confirm delivery. Choose contact and fulfillment Enter the requested contact details, address or pickup time. For delivery check zone, fee and offered slot; for preorder/tour links follow their specific deadline/date. The final checkout revalidates current rules and prices. Pay and verify confirmation Choose an offered payment method, review total and follow the secure payment flow. Wait for the verified order result. A rejected/pending payment is not a confirmed paid order; keep its reference and ask restaurant support before paying twice. Sign in before ordering Under Sign in, use Google or your email and password. Facebook and Apple appear only when configured. Standalone code sign-in is removed; address-verification and password-recovery codes remain separate. Older accounts without a password can use Forgot password to set one. Checkout offers the same configured providers alongside email/password; only the payment action submits inline enrollment. Guest access remains available, and card saving still needs separate consent. Access the new controls The entry sign-in invitation is controlled in Website → Order journey → Offer sign-in before ordering. Off goes directly to pickup/delivery details; when on, Order without an account remains immediately visible. Save the draft and publish to apply this choice. See the journey setting.

articles.title: Order from a table QR
articles.description: Scan the restaurant’s table QR and verify the displayed table before ordering.
articles.body: Scan the restaurant’s table QR and verify the displayed table before ordering. Join the correct table Open the signed QR link and follow the available session/guest flow. An expired or invalid link must be renewed by staff. Do not change table IDs or reuse another table’s link to bypass access. Order and request assistance Select items and required choices, review the basket and use the payment/ordering options enabled for this table. Use assistance controls when offered. Staff bill splitting and guest QR payments can have different capabilities; do not assume every POS action is available on the guest page.

articles.title: Track orders, receipts and saved methods
articles.description: Use the confirmation/tracking link or the restaurant’s order-history/account entry.
articles.body: Use the confirmation/tracking link or the restaurant’s order-history/account entry. Sign in before ordering At the start of the Pickup/Delivery dialog, choose Sign in or Continue as a guest below it. Both are text actions, without a filled sign-in button. No address field or confirmation button appears before this choice. Sign-in offers Google or email verification; closing it returns to the choices. The benefit text covers saved address/payment methods/orders for Delivery and saved details/payment methods/orders for Pickup. Continue as a guest reveals address entry for Delivery; Pickup shows collection details and menu access without asking for a delivery address. Back returns to the choices without clearing the draft. The guest choice is retained when switching services and closing/reopening this dialog. Signed-in customers proceed directly: a saved address with a validated selection offers Use this address and Edit. Incomplete addresses still require completion. Signing in after starting an address retains the draft. Saving a payment method remains a separate checkout choice. Sign in opens Google and the email/password form. Facebook and Apple appear only when configured by the service. Standalone email-code sign-in is no longer offered. Account creation, address verification and password-recovery codes remain separate. Read the current order state Open tracking and review the latest saved status and fulfillment information. Contact the restaurant for an operational change; the Foody help assistant cannot edit the order. Keep private tracking/receipt links out of public messages. Access history and receipts Complete the offered customer authentication/verification, then open the correct restaurant’s history. Select an order to view its digital receipt and available print/share/new-order actions. Reopening a receipt does not create a new order or payment. Manage payment enrollment If offered, explicitly opt into saving a payment method and complete the provider’s flow. Review the account’s saved-method state afterwards. Remove the Foody authorization through the account controls when needed; this does not cancel unrelated subscriptions with the provider. Check receipt and confirmation link previews Check that the restaurant has a name and logo configured, then share a valid receipt or order-confirmation link with its intended recipient. The link preview uses that restaurant’s name and logo, independently of the website’s general share image. Without a logo, the preview shows a card with the restaurant’s name. It does not include customer details, order lines or amounts. The linked page can still contain private order information: do not publish the link publicly. If the wrong identity appears, check that the link belongs to the intended restaurant and that its configured logo is accessible. An expired or invalid receipt cannot provide a restaurant preview. Choose a sign-in method Choose Google, Facebook or Apple when its button is offered, then complete authorization in the provider window. Cancellation does not replace the order draft. For email, enter your address and password under Sign in. If an older email-code account has no password, use Forgot password to set one after proving ownership; orders remain on that account. Creating an account may require address verification, and recovery still uses its separate code. Apple Hide My Email is supported. Switching providers does not guarantee account merging: if history is missing, use the original method and correct restaurant. A Facebook contact email never grants another account’s history. If a provider is absent or fails, use Google, password or guest access. Signing in does not consent to card storage. Understand sign-in data Configured providers may load their library when their choices are displayed and process browser/network information under their policy. Sign-in supplies Foody with a provider identifier and the supplied name, email or photo, not your Google, Apple or Facebook password. Apple may hide the email address. Foody keeps the session in an HttpOnly cookie and temporary authentication state; provider tokens are not persisted in Web Storage or these authentication logs. You can continue as a guest. To request account deletion, use the contact in Foody’s privacy policy; deletion is not a refund action.

articles.title: Availability (sold-out & low stock)
articles.description: Configure item stock, its availability rule and manual status in the current item editor.
articles.body: Items & menus → Item library → saved item → Stock & availability. Open Stock & availability For items still using persistent legacy stock, open a saved item from Items & menus → Item library and scroll to Stock & availability. The table shows the item, quantity and status. Editing requires menu editing permission. This section is part of the continuous editor, not a panel under a Recipe tab. Choose the stock basis For items still using persistent legacy stock, click the quantity or use Actions → Stock tracking. Track one shared item quantity or quantities by size, depending on its variants. Compatible items offer portions, g or kg. Without predefined item stock, calculation can use recipe ingredients and preparations. No recipe does not guarantee unlimited availability: also check predefined stock, variants, rules and manual status. Choose and manage a rule In stock tracking settings, choose an availability rule or the default rule. Actions → Manage rules opens Settings → Stock → Availability. Rules define tracking, low-stock threshold, out-of-stock behavior and remaining-count display. Check assignments before editing a rule used by multiple items. When the rule allows the remaining count to be shown, a stock of 20 portions caps that item’s total cart quantity at 20, even above the low-stock threshold. The low-stock badge still depends on the threshold. Stock is checked again when placing the order and may have changed meanwhile. An item overridden to Always available does not use this cap. Override status and save For items still using persistent legacy stock, click status and choose Follow a rule, Always available or Force sold out. Click Apply, then Save in the item header to persist it. Apply alone stages the change in the editor. The override wins over calculation; return to Follow a rule and save to resume automatic tracking. Check calculation and size quantities For items still using persistent legacy stock, actions → View availability calculation opens capacity details: possible sales, calculation basis and limiting ingredient when present. When tracking sizes separately, check each quantity. Item stock differs from recipe consumption quantities and the Active/Inactive filter in the Items library. An unavailable calculation is an error to investigate, not zero stock. Verify after saving After Save, reopen the item and check quantity, rule and status, then the relevant web or POS channel. Visibility also depends on groups, channels and hours. If rules fail to load, retry before saving; do not substitute an assumed configuration. Items and menus · Recipe quantities · Stock. Prepare stock for a new series With menu editing permission, open the rotating carte, select a series and open the “…” menu beside the title → Prepare stocks for this series. Enter INITIAL allowances including quantities already ordered: available = initial minus committed. Use shared units, compatible base measures (g/ml), counts per size, or no predefined limit. Copy previous initial quantities copies allowances, never previous remaining quantities or an old sold-out override. Quantities are shared by the same restaurant item across cartes for that series. Save draft keeps preparation private; Publish applies it atomically without restoring reservations made while editing. The first activation imports current available stock and existing scheduled orders, preserving current remaining quantities. Later series never inherit the old global counter. No predefined limit may still be constrained by a recipe, rule or manual status. Investigate stock changes Open Items & menus → Stock history. This page contains only the movement journal, visible as soon as it opens: it does not list current stock or offer corrections. Choose an Item or All Items, a Series date or All series, and a Movement or All movements. Past series dates are accepted. Filters combine and remain applied when using Show more. The journal shows the date and series, item, movement, before/after quantities and actor; a link opens the associated order when present. An empty result means no movements were recorded for those filters. Initial imports are labeled as imports; changes before tracking was activated cannot be reconstructed. If the item filter fails, Retry reloads that filter while the journal remains available. On a product, Full stock history opens this journal filtered to the item; Stock history opens its dialog. On a carte, the row History shortcut or its “…” menu also opens that dialog. To prepare or adjust initial series quantities, open the carte, choose the series, then Prepare stocks for this series, save the draft and publish after reviewing it. Availability actions marked immediate remain separate and journaled. A pre-production cancellation credits the original pool; a produced item remains consumed. If the journal fails to load, Retry reloads movements without changing filters; this error is not presented as an empty history. Manage a product tracked by series After series tracking is activated, Stock & availability shows the current series, available and committed quantities, Manage stock and Stock history. Use Manage stock to correct the selected series allowance. Its availability switch is immediate and journaled; it does not wait for the product Save button or carte publication. Use Automatic to resume its rule. Always available bypasses the stock cap and does not refill a counter. Product preparation settings and the availability rule remain part of the product save.

articles.title: Kitchen Companion: prep, service and closing
articles.description: Compatible activated iPad → More → Kitchen Companion
articles.body: Compatible activated iPad → More → Kitchen Companion Availability and access Native iPad/tablet layout and kitchen permissions are required; availability depends on activation. Prepare production objectives Review the selected service and proposed production quantities. Adjust allowed objectives and record actual preparation quantities using the corresponding controls. Review service priorities Open the service workspace to review availability and priorities. Treat simulation/projection results as planning aids and verify actual stock before making a production decision. Review sales and close the day Review sales links, counts, variance and preparation results. Save the review and use closing only after checking the figures; do not repeat a confirmed stock-changing closure. Use compatible Siri access On a supported activated iPad with the required system version and permissions, use the configured Siri/App Intents. If unavailable, use the app workspace; this is not Android voice support.

articles.title: Daily Operations
articles.description: Prepare service, review sales and stock, close/reopen a day, and explicitly generate and send supplier drafts.
articles.body: Kitchen → Today → Kitchen companion. Open the correct day Open Kitchen → Today, the Kitchen companion page. Select a date using the calendar and arrows; Today returns to the current day. Check restaurant and open/closed status. A historical day without a report differs from a loading error. Some production and receiving actions are offered only for the current day. Access and required data Changes require kitchen management permission and the relevant report controls. Configure recipes, units, prices and suppliers for useful calculations. Unmatched sales and missing recipes limit consumption/forecast coverage; they do not mean zero consumption. Prepare service In Prepare service, review preparations to launch, targets, sales forecasts and deliveries to check. A forecast is an estimate. Open a preparation and confirm production to record a batch; viewing a target or forecast produces nothing. Unavailable indicators show loading/error states, not reliable zero counts. During service During service compares preparation stock with a target entered for the next service. These targets are a local page simulation, not saved stock counts or supplier orders. Production requires a separate confirmation. Also review the sales journal and ingredients needing replenishment. Import, link and correct sales In Day review, open the journal, Import sales or Manual Sales Entry on an open report. Choose Foody POS or the offered external/Aviv file source, then review rows and item links. Do not manually duplicate sales already pulled from POS. Save manual quantities and check the result; link unmatched external products before interpreting consumption. Check and receive deliveries In Prepare service, Check delivery opens an expected purchase order. Check actually delivered quantities before confirming. Scan/import and quick receiving are separate actions. View recorded receipts in their drawer. Authorized deletion requires confirmation and can reverse the relevant movement; do not credit the same delivery twice through another import. Compare expected and counted stock Day review separates expected stock, physically counted quantities and variance. Use review filters/search, open an ingredient, enter its measured remaining quantity and confirm. Physical counts are optional: a missing count remains uncounted, not zero. Check the unit and saved result. Unmatched sales indicate incomplete coverage. Use the dedicated cost and recipe workspaces The review uses available sales, recipes and movements to explain variance. Cost/margin analysis and recipe imports have dedicated workspaces; do not look for the former charts or a recipe-import button inside this review. Food cost · Recipe Lab · Recipe quantities. Save the handover note Enter the handover note in Day review and use Save Draft after changes. This saves the note and recomputes the report; it does not close the day or send supplier orders. Wait for confirmation before changing date or leaving. Close the day Check sales, mappings and counts, then click Close Day and accept its confirmation. Closing recomputes/freezes the report, applies external/manual consumption not yet deducted and reconciles explicitly counted ingredients. Foody POS sales already deduct stock through the order flow and are not deducted again at close. Closing neither generates nor sends supplier orders. After an uncertain response, refresh and check closed status before another action. Reopen an eligible report Reopen day is offered for an eligible closed report, excluding historical-only imports. After confirmation, the server reverses deductions/count reconciliations belonging to that close and makes the report editable. Review sales/counts, then close again when appropriate. It does not recall supplier emails already sent. Explicitly generate estimated drafts On a closed report, open Estimated Supplies. Click All recorded sales, Aviv and manual sales or From POS to generate. Closing alone does not run generation. The calculation uses history, recipes and stock to suggest shortages grouped by supplier. It creates drafts without sending emails or orders. Review quantities, units and supplier; regeneration replaces previously generated drafts for that report. A forecast remains an estimate; diagnostics distinguish missing history, unlinked recipes and no shortages. Review and manually send Closing or generation never automatically sends a supplier order. Review the draft and requested delivery date; a delivery date/start is required for email. If missing, use the order’s send dialog in Kitchen → Purchases, fill Delivery date and start and complete the manual send there. If the date is already set, Send order in the estimated drawer opens the dialog: check the recipient, then click Send. Only this explicit action triggers email. Check status and result afterward; if uncertain after sending, verify before retrying. Purchases and orders. Recover after an error Distinguish empty results from load failures. If a confirmed save is followed by refresh failure, reload the result instead of repeating receipt, production, close or send. Preserve unsaved input before changing date. If sending remains uncertain, check the order and delivery outcome before transmitting again. Workflow and related guides Prepare service, receive deliveries, review sales/stock, save handover, then close. Separately generate and review supplier drafts; send only after manual confirmation. Stock · Preparations · Delivery import · Purchases. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Check the series stock journal Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Kitchen data and sales matching
articles.description: Admin → Kitchen → Data / POS → Kitchen data
articles.body: Admin → Kitchen → Data / POS → Kitchen data Inspect data coverage Open kitchen data and review the available catalog/recipe/sales matches. Distinguish missing data from a real zero quantity or cost. Correct a sales link Select the correct item/preparation for an unmatched sales entry and verify quantity/unit rules. Save and inspect the resulting report before relying on deductions or projections.

articles.title: Scan and review supplier deliveries
articles.description: Admin → Kitchen → Stock / Deliveries → import
articles.body: Admin → Kitchen → Stock / Deliveries → import Capture the document Choose the offered image/PDF/text/voice input and inspect the original document. Verify supplier/date and keep readable quantities and totals. Match products and units Match extracted lines to the correct stock products. Check package count, content unit, delivered quantity, price and VAT handling; never confirm solely from the AI suggestion. Resume a draft Save/resume a pending import when offered. Correct all unresolved lines before confirmation and verify whether a previous submission already created a delivery. Confirm once and check stock Confirm the reviewed delivery once, then inspect the delivery record and stock transaction history. Report discrepancies instead of importing the same document again.

articles.title: Food cost
articles.description: See the cost and margin of every dish, computed from its recipe, set a target, and find the dishes eating your profit.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. What Is It? Food cost tells you what each dish costs you to make and how much margin it leaves — computed automatically from its recipe and your stock prices . It's how you find the dishes quietly eating your profit. How It Works (Simply) The number comes straight from the chain you already set up: Stock prices ─┐ ├─→ Recipe (ingredients + preparations × quantities) ─→ Dish cost ─→ Margin vs its price Prep costs ─┘ So a dish only has a food cost once it has a recipe. No recipe = no cost (and the dish shows as un-costed). What you see Under Kitchen → Food Cost, inspect ingredient cost excluding VAT, selling price, cost percentage and margin for priced dishes. The chart has a 35% reference line; this is not an editable target on this page. Use search, status filter and sorting to inspect dishes. Missing recipe quantities or reliable costs prevent a reliable comparison. How to use it - Sort by food cost % to find your worst offenders first. - A dish costs too much? Adjust its portion or ingredients on the Recipe and cost section, change its price, or substitute a cheaper ingredient. - Prices changed? Update the ingredient in Stock; every dish using it re-costs automatically. Theoretical vs actual The Food cost page is your theoretical cost — what each dish should cost. To compare it against what you actually used (waste, over-portioning, errors), close the day in Daily operations; the variance is where money leaks. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Sale allowance is separate from recipe cost Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Preparations
articles.description: Sub-recipes you make in batches (sauces, doughs, marinades) and use across many dishes. Producing a batch credits stock; dishes that use it recover availability automatically.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. What Is It? A Preparation is a sub-recipe you make ahead in batches — a sauce, a dough, a marinade, a stock — and then use inside several dishes. Instead of listing raw ingredients on every dish, you point dishes at the preparation. How It Works (Simply) 1. Define the preparation in Kitchen → Preparations : its name, unit, and the raw ingredients one batch consumes (its recipe), plus the yield per batch (how much one batch produces). 2. Produce a batch when you make it. Foody deducts the raw ingredients from Stock and credits the produced quantity to the preparation. 3. Use it in dishes : on a dish's Recipe and cost section, add the preparation as an ingredient with the quantity one portion needs. Because dishes consume the preparation, its current quantity feeds straight into Availability: when a prep hits 0, dishes that use it go sold out — and the moment you produce a new batch, they come back. Why use them - Less duplication — change the sauce recipe once, every dish that uses it follows. - Accurate food cost — the prep's cost per unit rolls up from its ingredients and flows into each dish. - Real availability — "we're out of the green sauce" automatically 86's the right dishes. Example A tahini sauce yields 2 L per batch and costs ₪18 to make. Five dishes use 50 ml each. After producing one batch you can build ~40 portions; when it drops near zero those dishes show low stock , then sold out — until you produce another batch. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Keep preparation stock separate from sale allowances Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Recipe Lab and version review
articles.description: Admin → Kitchen → Lab
articles.body: Admin → Kitchen → Lab Start or import a recipe Choose manual entry, text import or an offered AI brief. Define the dish/objective, stock policy and relevant quantities before creating a draft. Validate ingredient links Review recipe components, existing/new stock and preparations. Resolve unit conversions and estimated prices; an estimated price is not a confirmed supplier purchase cost. Refine and review cost Use the refinement panel to propose changes, then inspect the recipe tree and cost summary. Verify preparation steps and image proposals before accepting them. Commit a reviewed version Select the intended menu item and commit only a validated draft. Use version history to inspect saved versions; check an uncertain commit before submitting it again.

articles.title: Stock Management
articles.description: Track raw ingredients, manage units and conversions, record transactions, import deliveries with AI, and get alerts when stock runs low.
articles.body: Kitchen → Stock: operational ingredient list, quantities and movements. Read the current stock list Stock shows a search/filter toolbar, Actions, Create item when permitted and an ingredient table. It no longer has the old Total Items, Low Stock and Inventory Value KPI cards. Value is shown per row and on the ingredient record, not in a summary card above the list. Search and filter by category or status Search by name. Category selects categories; Status offers Low Stock and OK. All Filters opens the combined filter panel. Criteria combine. Select Low Stock under Status to isolate ingredients needing restocking. Do not look for the old Low Stock Only checkbox. An empty filtered list is different from a loading error. Read columns and packaging levels The table includes name, category, quantity, price, total row value, supplier and status. Status flags Low Stock when the configured threshold is reached, otherwise showing the appropriate item state. Quantity and Price cells cycle available packaging display levels. This changes presentation, not stock. There is no gear column selector beside this page’s filters. An active ingredient with zero quantity also counts as Low Stock, even without a positive threshold. Create or edit an ingredient record With kitchen management permission, click Create item or open an existing row. The full-screen editor is continuous with a side summary; it does not have the old General and Packaging & Pricing tabs. Work through Identity & purchase, Purchase & price, Units and conversions, reorder threshold and Invoice names. Save commits the record. Enter identity, purchase and price Enter the order name, category, reference and supplier as needed. Under Purchase & price, describe the quantity and packaging actually bought, then the total price and requested VAT information. Supported forms cover a simple quantity, a container with contents, or packages containing multiple units. Check the base-unit summary before Save. Use Actions → price display to change list presentation excluding/including VAT; this does not alter recorded purchases. Understand units and conversions Base quantities use g, kg, ml, l or units. Packaging describes how they are bought: for example, 2 cartons × 12 cans × 400 g = 9.6 kg. Recipes use compatible units. Under Units and conversions, add a custom recipe unit with its equivalent base quantity and verify the conversion. Never infer a container’s contents from its name alone. Record a receipt, waste or adjustment Open the row action menu and choose the movement. Enter a positive quantity in the displayed unit and an optional note. Receive adds it; waste and manual adjustment subtract it. Check current and resulting stock before Confirm. If the movement saved but refresh failed, retry refresh rather than entering a second movement. Read history and understand variance The row History action shows up to 50 recent movements with type, quantity change, note and date. Distinguish receipts, waste and adjustments from consumption created by sales or production. A load error is not empty history. Compare theoretical and actual use for the relevant day in Daily Operations and check recipes and closing counts. Categories, selection and bulk actions Use row checkboxes to select records. Depending on permissions and selection, Actions offers category management, category or VAT updates, deletion and deselection. Category and Status filters limit the visible list; check selected rows before editing multiple records. Deletion confirmation is separate from filtering. Import a delivery and resume a draft From Actions, open Import delivery. Choose the supplier, upload the document and review extracted lines before confirming: matches to existing ingredients, units, packaging, quantities, prices and VAT. Analysis is not a confirmed receipt. Save a draft when needed and resume it from Supplies. Delivery-note import · Suppliers and purchases. Link ingredients to recipes In a saved item, Recipe and cost lets you add raw ingredients or preparations and enter quantities per serving or size. Stock record price and unit feed the calculation. Import a recipe from its recipe import action or Recipe Lab; this is not a bulk action of the Stock list. Recipe quantities · Recipe Lab. Check after changes After saving, check quantity, price, unit, status and effects on affected recipes. If image upload or refresh fails after a record was created, finish that step on the existing record without duplication. Align thresholds with your purchasing cycle and check the day before closing it. Units and stock settings · Daily Operations. Estimated supplies in Day review require explicit draft generation and a manual send; closing or generating does not transmit a supplier order. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Investigate predefined product stock Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Suppliers and purchase orders
articles.description: Admin → Kitchen → Purchases
