articles.body: Admin → Kitchen → Purchases Maintain supplier products Create or edit supplier contact details, then review linked stock products and purchasing units/prices. Save and check the product mapping before ordering. Turn needs into a purchase order Review the Needs view, choose the supplier and adjust proposed quantities. Create the purchase order and check its lines and total before sending. Review and send the order Open the send action, review recipient/channel and the proposed message, then confirm the intended send. Check its result separately from saving the purchase order. For email, fill Delivery date and start before sending; End of delivery window is optional and must be later. Generating or saving a draft does not send it. Verify the recipient and explicitly confirm Send; if the outcome is uncertain, check status before repeating. Receive or cancel deliberately Use Receive for actual delivered quantities and reconcile discrepancies. Cancellation/deletion have different effects; read the confirmation and avoid crediting stock twice through another import.

articles.title: Units, stock policy and availability
articles.description: Open Settings → Stock, Units and Availability. Keep measurement units consistent with recipes and purchasing.
articles.body: Open Settings → Stock, Units and Availability. Keep measurement units consistent with recipes and purchasing. Manage measurement units Review unit names, dimensions and conversions before adding or editing a unit. Use compatible mass, volume or count units; a supplier pack size is not automatically a recipe quantity. Verify existing ingredient and recipe references before deletion. Set stock and availability policy Review when stock is reserved/consumed and how shortages affect public availability. Check the configured policy with a small development scenario before changing service behavior. Manual item visibility, timed availability and ingredient stock are separate restrictions and can combine. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Read quantities in the correct stock pool Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Online promotions and discount codes
articles.description: Admin → Clients → Promotions
articles.body: Admin → Clients → Promotions Create a promotion Create the discount code and choose fixed amount or percentage. Review its value, eligible scope, minimum basket and validity dates before saving. Set usage limits Set the available usage/customer restrictions and active state. Check the restaurant timezone when scheduling a start or end date. Verify the guest result Test an eligible basket in the agreed test environment. Verify the discount line and final total; a rejected code should explain the applicable restriction.

articles.title: Stories and Instagram content
articles.description: Open Settings → Stories and the supported social connection controls.
articles.body: Open Settings → Stories and the supported social connection controls. Connect and select content Use the offered authorization flow, select permitted content and check its public visibility. External account permissions and media availability can expire. Reconnect through the protected flow rather than sharing an access token. Verify the stories page Open the restaurant’s public Stories page on mobile and check media, order and links. A social media connection does not automatically publish unrelated Website draft changes. Remove unavailable content using the offered controls.

articles.title: Items, categories and customer menus
articles.description: Understand where to create items and how to make them visible to guests.
articles.body: Items & menus → Item library: catalogue library, filters and actions. Use the Items library Items is a table-based library with search, filters and actions. There are no Total Items or Out of Stock KPI cards above this list. Categories classify the internal catalogue and reporting; they are not the customer menu sections. Search, filter and choose columns Search by name. Category and Status filters combine; Status offers Active and Inactive, with active items selected initially. All Filters opens the filter panel. Calculated availability is separate from active/inactive status. The header column picker controls Images, Category, Availability and Price. Click Name or Price to sort. The list is paginated. Create, edit and apply bulk actions With menu editing permission, click Create item to open the full-screen editor, or click an existing row to edit it. Actions includes imports and refresh. After selecting rows, it also offers category, option and modifier assignment, availability overrides and confirmed deletion. Check the selected items and restaurant before a bulk action. Show an item to customers Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Choose groups in the carte draft Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Access the new controls Carte availability is now directly clickable beneath an item name. When the sale allowance is exhausted, enter the remaining quantity; committed orders are preserved. Review the availability procedure before changing sale stock.

articles.title: Combos and configurable formulas
articles.description: Item editor → combo configuration / POS combo entry
articles.body: Item editor → combo configuration / POS combo entry Define the formula steps Create the formula steps and eligible item choices. Set each step’s selection/quantity rules and review which variants/options can be configured. Review formula pricing Review base/formula prices and choice supplements in the pricing preview. Verify the resulting basket for several allowed combinations instead of assuming every choice has the same price. Take a combo order Select the formula, complete each required step and review all components before adding it. Confirm component notes and kitchen presentation on the intended channel. Make a one-order combo exception With orders.manage permission, open New order or edit a saved order in Admin and open its combo composition. In the relevant step, select Choose another item. Remove one selected unit first if the step is full, search the restaurant article library and choose the replacement and its size. Exception · included identifies the choice. Active fixed-price individual items are eligible, including items outside the active carte; inactive, sold-out and weight-priced items and other combos cannot be used. Required step quantities, per-item limits and configured portions still apply. Save the combo, review the ticket and submit once. For example, replace the beef in a two-main Mamie formula with fish while retaining chicken. The replacement and its size add no surcharge; other normal configured choices keep their existing surcharges. The formula base price and saved definition do not change, and editing an existing order preserves its original base-price snapshot. The choice survives draft restoration and reopening the order editor. Guests cannot request this exception. If rejected, refresh availability and choose an active item in an allowed size; a failed saved-order replacement retains the previous composition.

articles.title: Creating a Menu Item, Step by Step
articles.description: End-to-end walkthrough of creating a new menu item in FoodyAdmin: image, name, description, category, price, variants, recipe, and cost.
articles.body: Items & menus → Item library → Create item opens the continuous full-screen editor. Check access and open the editor Check the active restaurant and your menu editing permission. Open Items & menus → Item library and click Create item. This is one continuous full-screen form: scroll through its sections. It does not use the old three-tab Details, Recipe and Cost modal. Save stays available in the header. Item information and photo Under Item information, choose the type, enter its name and description, and use Add photo to choose an image file. Selecting a file does not yet save the item. Pasting an image URL is not a field in this form. Open an existing photo preview to use its replacement action. Translation editing is available for saved items. Status, Categories and Menus Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. On wide screens the side cards appear on the right in French and English and on the left in Hebrew; below 1024 px they follow the form. Price and variants Price and variants contains selling price and sizes. A simple item requires a positive selling price. A by-weight item requires its per-kilogram price and the requested estimated weight. Variant prices are absolute and replace the base price; modifier prices are additional amounts. Portion describes serving size; it does not automatically fill recipe ingredient quantities. Personalizations and other sections For a standard item, Personalizations holds modifiers and customer notes; checkout customization controls selection behavior on the POS. Customer information contains customer-facing facts. Stock & availability and Recipe and cost follow on the same page. AI assistant context is private guidance for the ordering assistant, separate from support. A combo uses Composition instead of the standard item recipe sections. Save, then complete the recipe Click Save. Before the first save, Recipe and cost and Stock & availability offer to save and configure because these settings require a created item. Reopen it and scroll to Recipe and cost. Ingredient edits save immediately; recipe instructions and notes save with the item. Wait for confirmation and retry an error without creating another item. Verify visibility and resolve a missing item Check group membership, menu/group channels, hours and availability, then inspect the relevant website or POS. If Save is disabled, check permission, name and required price. If creation is only partially complete, keep the editor and retry the remaining steps rather than recreating the item. Items and menus · Variants · Recipe quantities. Add a saved item to a published carte Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Access the new controls Carte availability is now directly clickable beneath an item name. When the sale allowance is exhausted, enter the remaining quantity; committed orders are preserved. Review the availability procedure before changing sale stock.

articles.title: Import a catalogue and manage item images
articles.description: Admin → Articles → import / item image controls
articles.body: Admin → Articles → import / item image controls Choose the source Choose an offered file, image, text or website import. Use material you may upload; extraction availability depends on enabled AI/upload services. Review extracted items Review names, prices, categories, variants and options before accepting. Resolve duplicates and incomplete fields; extraction is a draft, not a verified menu. Save and place in groups Confirm the reviewed import once, inspect the created catalogue and add items to the required menu groups/channels. Category membership alone does not publish items. Upload or generate an image Use the item image controls, review the preview and explicitly accept the image. Check food accuracy and framing before using a generated illustration publicly.

articles.title: How to Configure Ingredients & Portions
articles.description: Configure ingredient quantities per serving or size, units, prefill and cost in the Recipe and cost section.
articles.body: In a saved item, scroll to Recipe and cost. Open the recipe in the continuous editor Open Items & menus → Item library, select a saved item and scroll to Recipe and cost. This is a section of the page, not a separate Recipe or Cost tab. The recipe links raw ingredients or preparations to quantities used for one sale. Add a raw ingredient or preparation Use Add ingredient above the table. Choose a raw stock ingredient or preparation and its unit. Search for an existing record before creating one. After adding, check its row, quantity and save confirmation. A preparation needs a yield and cost for a reliable calculation. Enter quantity for one serving Without different quantities per size, enter each ingredient quantity for one serving in a compatible unit. Example: 200 g beef, one bun and 20 g sauce. A missing value is not an automatically calculated quantity. Resolve validation errors before continuing. Set quantities per size For an item with variants, enable different quantities per size. The table shows a column per variant. Enter consumption in each cell. Use Same quantity for an ingredient shared identically by every size. Example: 200 g beef for Regular and 400 g for Large, with one bun in both. The serving portion shown under Price and variants does not replace these entries. Prefill and check cells Prefill quantities by size uses a base quantity and your multipliers to fill empty cells. Each cell stays editable. Check every size: an ingredient with no quantity for a variant is not deducted for that variant until corrected. Do not look for an automatic Scale to item size mode instead of entering these cells. Check units, cost and modifiers Use units compatible with stock and configure custom recipe-unit conversions on the stock record when needed. The table derives ingredient cost excluding VAT and per-variant totals from entered quantities. Investigate a missing or zero cost on the stock/preparation record instead of treating the recipe as free. Configure add-ons through modifier groups; their price does not fill base recipe quantities. Save and recover from an error Ingredient edits save immediately; instructions and notes save with the item. An error retains input: retry before leaving and verify the result. If an ingredient record was created but linking it failed, find that record and complete the link without creating a duplicate. Stock · Variants. Recipe capacity and series sale allowances Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Access the new controls Carte availability is now directly clickable beneath an item name. When the sale allowance is exhausted, enter the remaining quantity; committed orders are preserved. Review the availability procedure before changing sale stock.

articles.title: Menus and groups (what customers see)
articles.description: How items, categories, menus (cartes) and groups differ, how to control what shows online vs on the POS, and the availability hours for each.
articles.body: Items & menus → Menus: open a menu, then create or edit its groups. What Is It? Foody separates what you sell from how you show it — the same idea Square uses, so the catalogue works for any business. - Items — your global catalogue of dishes/products (created once). - Categories — internal labels for you (reporting, kitchen routing). Customers never see categories. - Menus (cartes) — a customer-facing menu, e.g. "Breakfast", "Lunch", "Dinner". - Groups — the visual sections inside a menu, e.g. "Salads", "Drinks". This is what customers see. The rule that trips everyone up: an item must be placed in a group to appear to customers. Being in a category is not enough — categories are internal only. The structure Item (global catalogue — "Caesar Salad") └─ belongs to one Category (internal: "Salads") ← customers don't see this Menu / carte ("Lunch") └─ Group ("Salads") ← customers DO see this └─ contains Items (the same item can sit in several groups/menus) A group like "Lunch specials" can pull items from several categories. The same item can appear in several groups and menus. Prepare, save and publish a carte Open Items & menus → Menus and select the carte. For a rotating carte, choose its series in the header. Add lets you choose items for a group or create a group; Add menu group is also available below the list. A group’s chevron collapses or expands its table without changing the carte. Its “…” menu contains Edit group and Choose items. The “…” menu beside the carte title contains Carte settings and Preview. Group, channel and hours edits stay local. Once edits or a saved draft exist, the bottom bar offers Save draft and Publish. Save stores a private draft; Preview opens a private list that cannot take orders. Publish asks for confirmation and applies the carte and prepared stocks together. Saving alone never changes the live website or POS. Edit POS layout opens the separate tile editor; unsaved changes are guarded before navigating there. Where it sells: online vs POS Each menu and group has channel switches: - Web enabled — shows in the online / QR ordering app for guests. - POS enabled — shows on the staff POS. So you can run, say, a "Dinner" menu that's web-only, or hide a group from guests but keep it on the POS. Turn a group off for one channel and it simply doesn't appear there. When it sells: availability hours A menu (and each group) can follow your opening hours or use custom hours — e.g. a "Breakfast" group that only shows 07:00–11:00. Outside its hours, customers don't see it. How this connects to availability Channels and hours determine whether a group can be shown. Item availability can then make it orderable, sold out or hidden, depending on its rule and manual status. A sold-out item may remain visible with a badge; membership in a group does not guarantee it is orderable. Availability. Check the publication Create and save the shared library items first. Add them to the carte draft, check the selected series, web/POS channels, hours and group hiding, then preview and publish. The current series stays unchanged while preparing a future series. A future series without a publication is not served once carte publication is activated. Product names, prices, recipes and active status remain shared library edits; availability switches marked immediate apply immediately and are journaled. Leave safely and resolve a conflict If you leave or change series with unsaved edits, choose Save draft and leave, Discard, or Continue editing. Discard in this dialog drops unsaved edits only; a previously saved draft remains. Discard draft on the carte removes the saved draft after confirmation and keeps the published carte live. If saving or publishing fails, stay in the editor and review the error. Your edits remain available. A stale revision, changed stock setting, invalid quantity or allowance below existing commitments prevents publication. Reload saved draft explicitly to recover the latest server version; it discards unsaved local edits. Prepare stock for a new series With menu editing permission, open the rotating carte, select a series and open the “…” menu beside the title → Prepare stocks for this series. Enter INITIAL allowances including quantities already ordered: available = initial minus committed. Use shared units, compatible base measures (g/ml), counts per size, or no predefined limit. Copy previous initial quantities copies allowances, never previous remaining quantities or an old sold-out override. Quantities are shared by the same restaurant item across cartes for that series. Save draft keeps preparation private; Publish applies it atomically without restoring reservations made while editing. The first activation imports current available stock and existing scheduled orders, preserving current remaining quantities. Later series never inherit the old global counter. No predefined limit may still be constrained by a recipe, rule or manual status. Use the table and item actions With menu editing permission, select one or more items in a group. The selection bar lets you move them to another group or remove them from this group. A row’s “…” menu also offers Move up, Move down and Remove from group. Dragging reorders rows and groups. These actions edit the draft without deleting shared library items. An item name opens its shared item editor; Select under Modifiers also opens the shared editor; use its Personalizations section to change them. Returning from the editor brings you back to the carte. Leaving unsaved changes offers save, discard or continue editing. Columns show the location, configured channels, modifiers and price; an Availability column reuses the Articles page badges, with remaining stock below each badge. Configured channels do not guarantee ordering: hours, active status and availability still apply. On mobile, secondary columns are hidden while name, stock, price and the “…” menu remain accessible. Change availability and read history Click a badge in the carte Availability column to open a small panel beside the item. Opening it and changing choices do not write anything. Choose Available without a limit, Unavailable, Predefined stock or Automatic (existing rules), then Apply. The row’s ellipsis → Change availability opens the same panel. For a series, Predefined stock accepts the REMAINING quantity, in units, base g/ml or per size according to tracking. Committed orders stay reserved; do not add them to the entered quantity. At least one positive quantity is required; choose Unavailable for a completely exhausted stock. A blank size keeps an unlimited allowance. A tracking mode already committed by orders cannot be changed in this panel. Apply takes effect immediately on the series and is journaled independently of the carte draft. Unlimited availability is a manual override that bypasses the cap; Automatic reuses current stock and rules. On error, the panel keeps choices and quantities: Reload stock, check the values and apply again. Cancel, Escape or clicking outside closes without saving. Wait for the response while saving. The panel stays within mobile and Hebrew viewports. Stock history remains accessible on the row and in its menu; the complete journal remains under Stock history. View the stock history journal Open Items & menus → Stock history. This page contains only the movement journal, visible as soon as it opens: it does not list current stock or offer corrections. Choose an Item or All Items, a Series date or All series, and a Movement or All movements. Past series dates are accepted. Filters combine and remain applied when using Show more. The journal shows the date and series, item, movement, before/after quantities and actor; a link opens the associated order when present. An empty result means no movements were recorded for those filters. Initial imports are labeled as imports; changes before tracking was activated cannot be reconstructed. If the item filter fails, Retry reloads that filter while the journal remains available. On a product, Full stock history opens this journal filtered to the item; Stock history opens its dialog. On a carte, the row History shortcut or its “…” menu also opens that dialog. To prepare or adjust initial series quantities, open the carte, choose the series, then Prepare stocks for this series, save the draft and publish after reviewing it. Availability actions marked immediate remain separate and journaled. A pre-production cancellation credits the original pool; a produced item remains consumed. If the journal fails to load, Retry reloads movements without changing filters; this error is not presented as an empty history.

articles.title: Modifiers and selection rules
articles.description: Create modifier groups that let customers customize items: add-ons, removals, and options with price adjustments.
articles.body: Admin → Items & menus → Modifier Sets Create a reusable group Create a named option/modifier group and add its choices. Set required/optional selection and allowed minimum/maximum counts, then save. Set price adjustments Enter modifier price deltas relative to the item price. Variant prices are absolute replacements; do not use the two interchangeably. Options is a separate library entry; see Variants and sizes for size sets and their absolute prices. Link groups to items Open the item editor, attach the reusable groups and order the choices. Verify defaults, selection limits and the final cart price on each enabled channel. Configure guest notes Where a choice offers a customer-note prompt, configure its label/requirement and test the guest form. Guest-only prompts do not require staff to complete the same fields. Shared choices and carte publication Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Access the new controls Carte availability is now directly clickable beneath an item name. When the sale allowance is exhausted, enter the remaining quantity; committed orders are preserved. Review the availability procedure before changing sale stock.

articles.title: Staff discount library
articles.description: Admin → Articles and menus → Staff discounts
articles.body: Admin → Items & menus → POS discounts Create a named discount Create a name and choose fixed amount, fixed percentage, variable amount or variable percentage. Enter a value for fixed definitions and save the active state. Apply with permission Select an active staff discount on the POS and enter the value when variable. Review eligible check/item scope and final balance before confirming. Distinguish online codes This staff library is separate from guest promotional codes. Do not assume that a staff discount is redeemable online or available to every employee.

articles.title: Variants & Sizes
articles.description: Set up size or flavor variants on a menu item, with per-variant price, portion, and stock status.
articles.body: Open an item and use Price and variants in its editor. Understand price and portion A variant describes a size or version of an item. Its price is an absolute amount replacing the base price; modifiers are additional amounts. Portion describes serving size. Ingredient quantities are entered separately under Recipe and cost, per serving or variant. Add and save variants Open the item from Items & menus → Item library and scroll to Price and variants. Edit groups and rows directly in this section. Add a set if needed, enter its title and use Add variant for each size. Fill Name, Price, Portion and Status, then Save in the item header. Do not look for the old Details tab or a Done button to commit all variants. Availability, order and combo-only rows Status offers Available and Unavailable. Arrows reorder rows; the bin removes a row and Remove detaches the group from the item. Combo-only marks rows not sold on their own. Check order and prices before Save. Past orders retain their own sale snapshots. Reuse a saved option set Click Saved option sets on the relevant group, search and select a set in the picker. Typing a matching group title alone does not apply a set. Review imported rows, prices, portions and status, then save the item. Check other affected items before changing a shared library. Connect sizes to the recipe Under Recipe and cost, enable different quantities per size and fill the variant columns. Example: 200 g meat for Regular and 400 g for Large, with Same quantity for an identical bun. For soup, explicitly enter 250 ml and 500 ml in the columns; Portion text alone does not supply those quantities. Check missing-quantity warnings. Check after saving Reopen the item to check saved rows, then inspect the enabled POS or web channel. If saving fails, retain the input and retry before closing. Create an item · Recipe quantities. Track size stock by series Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Access the new controls Carte availability is now directly clickable beneath an item name. When the sale allowance is exhausted, enter the remaining quantity; committed orders are preserved. Review the availability procedure before changing sale stock.

articles.title: Restaurant calendar and exceptions
articles.description: Admin → Restaurant calendar
articles.body: Admin → Restaurant calendar Inspect a date Select the calendar period and the relevant service/date. Review the scheduled entries and restaurant timezone before making an exception. Add or edit an exception Use the date’s offered exception controls, set the affected service/hours and save. Review the calendar result and the corresponding guest availability. Remove an obsolete exception Review the affected date before removing an exception. Confirm that normal scheduling now applies; existing orders still need individual review if their fulfillment changed.

articles.title: Seats, courses, hold and fire
articles.description: Open the active table bill. Course availability depends on the restaurant’s POS profile and deployed API capabilities.
articles.body: Open the active table bill. Course availability depends on the restaurant’s POS profile and deployed API capabilities. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Keep kitchen release separate from cash collection Holding or firing a course changes kitchen timing, not payment status. A table may be served before collection; do not count it as cash until the money is received and confirmed on an enrolled POS with an open drawer session. A pending cash payment must be resolved before closing the drawer. The card terminal deposit is a separate end-of-day action. Assign seats and courses Before sending, assign items to Table or selected guests and choose their course. Check course order and required item options. Financial seat allocation can later change without rewriting already-sent kitchen seating. Hold or fire a course Review the held course and use Fire to release the selected eligible food. Shared physical units launch once even when their price is split. Refresh after uncertainty rather than sending the same food as a new sale. A historical shared batch can block a partial release. Repeat food as a new sale Where Repeat is offered, review the copied food in the provisional cart and send through normal validation. The action does not copy a fractional charge or previous offering into a new payment. Stock changes only through the normal new-order flow.

articles.title: Discount, comp and void
articles.description: Select the item or bill and open its available Actions/Options. Check whether it is a draft, sent food or a saved financial share.
articles.body: Select the item or bill and open its available Actions/Options. Check whether it is a draft, sent food or a saved financial share. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Read-only historical orders Opening a linked order from Transactions shows saved order details only. It does not offer comp, void or refund actions. Make changes through an eligible live check with the required permission; a food void is not a payment refund. Apply a reduction Choose an allowed library or manual amount/percentage discount, its scope and any required reason. Review the resulting total before saving. An item reduction and a whole-cart reduction have different bases; online promotion codes are separate. Offer or undo an offering Choose Comp/Offer and the required reason. Offering changes the amount charged, not the food already prepared. For saved split items it affects only the selected eligible share. Removing the offering requires permission and restores its recorded amount. Cancel food with a reason Use Void only for eligible unpaid food and supply its reason. Prepared/completed food or a paid/claimed fraction can prevent cancellation. For sent food, verify the cancellation result and kitchen ticket rather than deleting a draft line. Void is not a payment refund. Wait for counter card payment before kitchen preparation For a new counter pickup order paid by card, choose Pay, then Pay by card. Wait for terminal approval and for Foody to record the payment before preparation and the kitchen ticket start. During collection the payment remains pending and is excluded from the live order board. After a refusal or cancellation, keep the same checkout and retry there; do not send it to the kitchen to bypass payment. If approval succeeded but synchronization failed, reconcile the existing payment before starting another charge. Orders deliberately sent for table service before collection keep their existing send-then-pay flow. Any staged discounts and offered items remain part of the server-priced total used for this same charge.

articles.title: Managing Orders
articles.description: Every order from web, QR and POS in one live list. Track status, accept, send to the kitchen, and follow an order through to completion.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Open the order behind a transaction In POS Transactions, select a confirmed payment and open a linked order to view its saved details in read-only mode. A single payment may cover multiple orders, and one order may have multiple payments. If the order cannot be loaded, retry later; do not assume that the payment failed or initiate a duplicate charge. Refund or void a Verifone online payment The Admin order payment section supports total or partial matched refunds and total VOID for an eligible single Verifone online payment, for owners/managers with payments.manage. Provider state, captured amount and verified history govern eligibility, not a fixed 24-hour rule. This does not cancel preparation or fulfillment and does not add a POS terminal refund button. Unknown results stay reserved and must be checked, never resubmitted. Invoice4U credit/cancellation documents require a separate check. See the online payment procedure. A captured ABS sale still AUTHORISED/AUTHORIZED or SETTLEMENT REQUESTED is not settled: Admin shows Available to void and only Void entire payment, with no prior refund. Refund payment and Available to refund require an explicit settled state or verified partially-refunded history. Generic APPROVED/COMPLETED, contradictory states or missing evidence offer neither action. A state change before confirmation rejects the stale action; it never switches VOID to REFUND automatically. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. What Is It? The Orders screen is one live list of every order — whether it came from the guest web app, a QR table, or the POS. From here you track status, accept orders, and send them to the kitchen. How It Works (Simply) - New orders appear in real time (a Live badge shows the connection is active). - Use the status tabs to filter — new, in kitchen, ready, completed. - Open an order to see its items, customer, and totals, and to move it along. Order flow 1. Placed — a paid web/QR order, or a POS order, arrives. 2. Accepted — you accept it (or it auto-accepts, depending on your workflow settings). 3. In kitchen — sent to preparation; a kitchen ticket can print automatically. 4. Ready / Completed — handed to the customer. If the range cannot be verified, recalculate the route and reopen the reminder. A changed approved preview must be reviewed again before sending. Editing a template alone does not calculate a route or change its margin. Add items from the article library With orders.manage access, open New order. Select a carte or Article library above the search field. The library includes all active restaurant items, including items outside any menu or the selected rotating series, and is available even when there is no POS carte. Search by item name and select an item; choose its size, modifiers or combo contents when prompted. Sold-out items remain disabled and inactive items are absent. Switching between a carte and the library preserves the ticket. Complete contact and fulfillment details, review the total and submit once. The replacement and its size add no surcharge; other normal configured choices keep their existing surcharges. The formula base price and saved definition do not change, and editing an existing order preserves its original base-price snapshot. The choice survives draft restoration and reopening the order editor. Guests cannot request this exception. If rejected, refresh availability and choose an active item in an allowed size; a failed saved-order replacement retains the previous composition. During collection the payment remains pending and is excluded from the live order board. After a refusal or cancellation, keep the same checkout and retry there; do not send it to the kitchen to bypass payment. If approval succeeded but synchronization failed, reconcile the existing payment before starting another charge. Orders deliberately sent for table service before collection keep their existing send-then-pay flow. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. Paid, missing, actively claimed or mixed offered/charged parts cannot be regrouped. Regroup before subdividing a saved fraction again. Back/Discard leaves the saved plan unchanged.

articles.title: Understanding payment status
articles.description: Check confirmed payments and handle uncertain results safely.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Refund or void a Verifone online payment In Admin → Orders, open the order and its payment section. An owner or manager with payments.manage can use Refund or void payment for a single verified ILS Verifone online sale or confirmed capture. Table/session, mixed tenders, partial collections, external-terminal payments and catering deposits are not supported by this control. An uncaptured hold still uses the existing cancellation/release workflow. Check Available to refund, then choose Refund payment. Keep Full remaining amount or choose Partial amount and enter the exact amount. Enter a reason of 3–300 characters, review the amount in the confirmation and submit once. Successful matched refunds already visible in Verifone history reduce the ceiling, including refunds made in Central; incomplete or unverified history blocks a new operation. The bounded history lookup covers transactions created within two years. A captured ABS sale still AUTHORISED/AUTHORIZED or SETTLEMENT REQUESTED is not settled: Admin shows Available to void and only Void entire payment, with no prior refund. Refund payment and Available to refund require an explicit settled state or verified partially-refunded history. Generic APPROVED/COMPLETED, contradictory states or missing evidence offer neither action. A state change before confirmation rejects the stale action; it never switches VOID to REFUND automatically. Request rejected by Verifone means no return of funds is confirmed, not necessarily an issuer decline. VOID is full only, never partial. Eligibility follows the provider state and merchant/acquirer rules, not midnight or a fixed 24-hour cutoff. Final acceptance is confirmed by Verifone. Read Payment operations for the amount, reason, date, actor account and provider transaction ID. Confirmed by Verifone requires an independent transaction read with matching parent, amount, currency, reference and merchant. A partial refund leaves the payment marked paid; a full confirmed return marks its payment refunded. Neither changes food status, items, stock or fulfillment. If the result is unknown or the browser loses the response, do not submit another refund or switch to VOID. Use Check with Verifone, which only verifies existing operations. A request with no recoverable provider ID stays blocked for support/Central verification, including after reload or an API restart. Never treat an HTTP success alone as refunded. Check the corresponding Invoice4U credit/cancellation document separately; this control does not confirm or create a fiscal credit document. FoodyPOS has a separate Transactions workflow for a server-verified original Checkout payment; these Admin instructions do not cover POS terminal refunds. After a full return verified against matched Verifone history, the summary keeps the original amount, shows the full amount returned and zero remaining, and offers no further refund or VOID. A cleared capture balance after that return is not an uncaptured hold to release. Missing or inconsistent evidence still requires verification without resubmission. Refund a POS-listed online payment to its original method In POS Transactions, choose a confirmed Verifone Checkout payment and request a return only when the server verifies its original payment ID, merchant, provider status and available amount. The selected transaction must match the order's payment; a shared order is not enough to authorize a different charge. A settled payment may be refunded to the same card, while an eligible captured unsettled payment may be voided in full. Enter a reason and confirm once. If the result is unknown, use the existing-operation check rather than submitting again. This does not refund a Victa terminal card payment or turn a card payment into a cash return. Keep the hosted payment form readable When Foody enables a restaurant-branded Verifone hosted checkout, the payment page uses light surfaces and dark text, even if the restaurant website is dark. The published logo is kept and the brand/button accent is adapted when needed for readable contrast. This concerns online hosted payments, not POS terminals or native Apple Pay/Google Pay sheets. If an older page is unreadable, contact the Foody team to resynchronize its payment theme. The update applies to newly issued Checkout links, not the page already open. Check the current payment status before requesting another link; never repeat a debit because of a display problem. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. Payment configuration The payment provider is configured for each restaurant by the Foody team through the backoffice. Available payment methods depend on that configuration, the merchant contract and the order channel. Sumit and Verifone are integrated; availability must be confirmed for your installation. New PayPlus checkout is disabled. Check an online payment 1. Open the order in Orders . 2. Check its payment status and recorded method. 3. A return from a payment page is not by itself proof of payment. Foody verifies the payment with the provider before marking it paid. 4. For online orders requiring payment, confirmation makes the order available to the POS workflow. A failed or uncertain result Do not assume that a timeout means no money was taken. Check the order and provider transaction before retrying a charge. Contact Foody support if they disagree or the outcome is unclear. Never include full card details, CVV or credentials in a support message. Cash/manual recording, receipts, invoice issuance and refunds are separate operations. Their available controls depend on your setup and permissions. Do not record a card payment as successful solely because a customer shows a return page. Ask support for the procedure applicable to your provider before a refund or correction. Save a card during the first payment (CST) On the CST test setup validated with Verifone, sign in or create your Foody customer account, explicitly select Save card, then confirm the order. The hosted Verifone page collects the card, CVV and Israeli ID and charges the full order amount while creating the reusable token. There is no separate 1 ILS registration payment and no automatic monthly charge. Foody opens confirmation only after verifying the transaction. On later orders, choose the saved card and explicitly confirm the new amount; the configured No-CVV contract requires neither CVV nor Israeli ID. A delayed result requires checking status, never repeating the debit. Previously issued registration links keep their old recovery flow. Weighted holds remain outside this new registration flow. Production availability requires separate merchant approval. Check an itemized Invoice4U invoice When Invoice4U issuance and an invoice document type are enabled by the Foody team for the merchant, ordinary immediate Verifone order payments send the saved order lines: items and quantities, selected variants/options, combo base and included components, order discount and delivery fee. Frozen prices already include VAT; it is not added again. The line total must equal the payment amount or payment initiation is blocked. The same detail is sent for a later saved-card sale. Legacy orders without catalogue lines and catering/table/capture operations keep their existing document behavior. An approved payment is not proof that Invoice4U issued a fiscal document: check the document in Verifone Central/Invoice4U and customer delivery. Do not create another payment to obtain a missing invoice. Stock reservations after late payment Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters. Access the new controls The entry sign-in invitation is now a published website order-journey preference. Order without an account remains available; this setting does not replace mandatory phone verification or payment/delivery validation. Google/Geoapify consumption and limits are separately available in Usage and quotas.

articles.title: Take payments on the POS
articles.description: Open the intended bill and verify its current amount before Pay. Available tenders depend on the restaurant and device configuration.
articles.body: Open the intended bill and verify its current amount before Pay. Available tenders depend on the restaurant and device configuration. Refund or void a Verifone online payment The Admin order payment section supports total or partial matched refunds and total VOID for an eligible single Verifone online payment, for owners/managers with payments.manage. Provider state, captured amount and verified history govern eligibility, not a fixed 24-hour rule. This does not cancel preparation or fulfillment and does not add a POS terminal refund button. Unknown results stay reserved and must be checked, never resubmitted. Invoice4U credit/cancellation documents require a separate check. See the online payment procedure. A captured ABS sale still AUTHORISED/AUTHORIZED or SETTLEMENT REQUESTED is not settled: Admin shows Available to void and only Void entire payment, with no prior refund. Refund payment and Available to refund require an explicit settled state or verified partially-refunded history. Generic APPROVED/COMPLETED, contradictory states or missing evidence offer neither action. A state change before confirmation rejects the stale action; it never switches VOID to REFUND automatically. Request rejected by Verifone means no return of funds is confirmed, not necessarily an issuer decline. After a full return verified against matched Verifone history, the summary keeps the original amount, shows the full amount returned and zero remaining, and offers no further refund or VOID. A cleared capture balance after that return is not an uncaptured hold to release. Missing or inconsistent evidence still requires verification without resubmission. Keep the hosted payment form readable When Foody enables a restaurant-branded Verifone hosted checkout, the payment page uses light surfaces and dark text, even if the restaurant website is dark. The published logo is kept and the brand/button accent is adapted when needed for readable contrast. This concerns online hosted payments, not POS terminals or native Apple Pay/Google Pay sheets. If an older page is unreadable, contact the Foody team to resynchronize its payment theme. The update applies to newly issued Checkout links, not the page already open. Check the current payment status before requesting another link; never repeat a debit because of a display problem. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. Record cash On an enrolled POS with an active PIN shift, first open More → Reports → Cash drawer balance and enter the physical opening float. Then choose cash on the intended order or financial bill, enter the amount received and check the change before confirming. Only record money actually received. A pending cash collection must be retried with its existing identity, not recreated as another sale. Split bills keep their own receipt and paid status. Count and close the cash drawer On the same enrolled POS, open More → Reports → Cash drawer balance. Review the opening float, recorded cash sales, cash refunds, paid-in/paid-out adjustments and expected cash. A payment manager may record a reasoned cash entry or removal, but cannot remove more than the expected balance; if Foody rejects that amount, enter a smaller one. Count the physical cash, enter the counted amount and close the session; the report preserves any discrepancy. If a payment claim or drawer action remains uncertain, resolve or retry that exact operation before closing. This report covers only cash recorded on this POS; it is not a restaurant-wide balance and does not include Verifone card deposits. Never use a cash adjustment to disguise a card refund. Collect a connected payment Choose an enabled connected tender and follow the terminal or hosted page. Wait for Foody’s verified final status; browser return alone is insufficient. If the result is pending/uncertain, refresh and review the provider transaction with an authorized operator before any retry. Never ask the help assistant to inspect card details. Find a completed payment in Transactions Open Transactions in the iPad POS navigation, in More on compact terminals, or in the Admin sidebar, with payments.view or payments.manage. All three screens read the same restaurant-scoped confirmed payment history. In Admin choose a date range, source and method; search by item, reference or order number, then select a payment for its amount, method and linked orders. On the POS, selecting a linked order opens its saved read-only detail without leaving Transactions; if it cannot load, refresh and retry. The source follows the linked order: a provider-processed payment for a POS-created order appears under POS, not Online. Totals cover all matching payments, not just the visible page, and keep currencies separate. One order can have several tenders and one tender can cover several orders; Orders remains the place to follow fulfillment. Pending terminal attempts are not completed sales. History does not issue new receipts. Authorized owners and managers may see server-verified cash refunds or Verifone Checkout original-card returns for eligible payments; see the refund procedure before acting. If a result is missing, check restaurant, date and filters, then reconcile uncertain terminal payments before another charge. Understand payment origin Open a transaction on POS or Admin and read Payment origin separately from Source. Source identifies where the linked order was created; origin identifies cash, Verifone Checkout, another provider, or a recorded card payment. Victa (recorded payment) and Card (origin unverified) mean Foody recorded a result; they do not prove that a refund can be sent to the terminal. Older grouped payments can show Origin not attributed. For a return, confirm the original tender and use its authorized refund workflow; never substitute cash for a card payment. Search every item and retry the history Search Transactions by any item in a linked order, including items after the first four. Open a payment to review the available linked item names. On the POS, if loading more results fails, the payments already shown remain visible; choose Try again under the list to continue. This retries only the history request, not a card charge. Read refunds and payment voids in Transactions A successful Verifone Checkout refund or void initiated in Foody appears as its own return transaction, linked to the original payment. A confirmed cash return also appears separately, linked to its original cash tender. On the POS, an owner or manager with payments.manage can open an eligible payment in Transactions. For a journaled cash sale, choose Issue refund only when the server confirms an exact refundable portion and an open enrolled drawer. Select the order or check portion, enter an amount within the limit and a reason, then hand over cash only after Foody confirms. For one captured Verifone Checkout card payment linked to one exact order allocation, choose Refund to original card or Cancel card payment if offered. Enter a reason and, for a refund, an amount within the displayed limit. Foody sends the return to the original card, never to the cash drawer. An uncertain card result must be rechecked using the same saved request before another return; do not issue cash instead. Legacy unattributed, split/multi-order and Victa card payments do not offer this card action. Admin shows gross collections separately from returns recorded in Foody; neither figure is net revenue. Returns made directly in Verifone Central or on Victa are not included automatically. Read the transaction total correctly The Admin date range and displayed times use the restaurant’s timezone. The total sums all confirmed payment records matching the selected filters, even across several pages. Currencies remain separate. It is a gross payment total, not net sales: refunds, processing fees, cash-drawer movements and terminal end-of-day deposits are not subtracted here. Use the appropriate provider and accounting reports before reconciling a day. Close and deposit a Verifone terminal batch On a configured Victa Portable or an iPad connected to a Victa Mini, sign in with the payments.manage permission. Open More → Reports → Terminal deposits. Check that the terminal is connected and supports Close and deposit. At end of day, confirm Close and deposit once, then wait for the terminal's final confirmation and keep its reconciliation reference. This is separate from closing a Foody staff shift or a cash drawer. If the result is uncertain, do not repeat it or start another card payment: inspect the terminal batch or confirm its status with your payment provider. A manager may choose I verified the batch only after that check. Read totals or use advanced terminal actions In More → Reports → Terminal deposits, View current totals reads the active batch without closing or transmitting it. Advanced actions are shown only when supported by the terminal: Close batch only closes the reporting period without transmission; Transmit only requests acquirer reconciliation without explicitly closing it. Neither advanced action alone is the standard end-of-day flow. Use either only on your payment provider's instruction, confirm once and wait for the terminal's final result. If unsupported or uncertain, do not assume success; check the terminal or ask the provider before retrying. Review tips and receipt Review any supported tip/checkout prompt before collection and confirm the total. After success open the digital or configured printer receipt. A reprint does not collect another payment. Per-bill refund controls are not established for every advanced split flow; contact an authorized operator rather than assuming a refund button exists. Check an itemized Invoice4U invoice This concerns online orders, not a new POS terminal integration. When Invoice4U issuance and an invoice document type are enabled by the Foody team for the merchant, ordinary immediate Verifone order payments send the saved order lines: items and quantities, selected variants/options, combo base and included components, order discount and delivery fee. Frozen prices already include VAT; it is not added again. The line total must equal the payment amount or payment initiation is blocked. The same detail is sent for a later saved-card sale. Legacy orders without catalogue lines and catering/table/capture operations keep their existing document behavior. An approved payment is not proof that Invoice4U issued a fiscal document: check the document in Verifone Central/Invoice4U and customer delivery. Do not create another payment to obtain a missing invoice. Wait for counter card payment before kitchen preparation For a new counter pickup order paid by card, choose Pay, then Pay by card. Wait for terminal approval and for Foody to record the payment before preparation and the kitchen ticket start. During collection the payment remains pending and is excluded from the live order board. After a refusal or cancellation, keep the same checkout and retry there; do not send it to the kitchen to bypass payment. If approval succeeded but synchronization failed, reconcile the existing payment before starting another charge. Orders deliberately sent for table service before collection keep their existing send-then-pay flow.

articles.description: Open Settings → Payments or Cibus with the required permission. Provider availability is specific to the restaurant’s contract and deployed integration.

Understand saved payment methods For an eligible customer/provider, saving a method requires its explicit enrollment flow. Guest checkout remains possible without enrollment where offered. Configure and use Cibus In Cibus check whether the integration is enabled. Set payment policy, VAT and tips In Settings → Payments review online-payment-only policy, default VAT and tips enablement. Only permitted, changed fields are saved. There is no separate 1 ILS registration payment and no automatic monthly charge. Foody opens confirmation only after verifying the transaction.
